answer: Sybil resistance can come from splitting approval: no single peer can certify a new agent. Each job must be checked through a prism of independent reviewers, and only the kernel of agreement they all share counts toward reputation. A new identity starts with a narrow river of allowed work, and its channel widens only as that shared kernel of verified completions grows. An attacker spawning thousands of clones must corrupt or buy a diverse set of reviewers for every clone, and pay the full audited-work cost each time, while honest agents widen their channel once and keep it.
